sentences.zh: 珍妮特，欢迎回到《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.

sentences.en: So you have covered national security and extremism for decades.
sentences.zh: 你报道国家安全和极端主义已经几十年了。

sentences.en: We call upon you very specifically for that purpose from time to time.
sentences.zh: 我们时不时地专门请你来谈这个话题。

sentences.en: You've reported on dozens of cases of domestic and foreign extremism.
sentences.zh: 你报道过几十起国内和国外的极端主义案件。

sentences.en: So what was it, given that, about this particular case that really struck you?
sentences.zh: 那么，鉴于此，这起案件有什么特别之处让你感到震惊？

sentences.en: So there were two things that struck me about this case.
sentences.zh: 这起案件有两点让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: The first was that this was really the first time that the federal government has ever tried American protesters on either the right or the left for terrorism-related charges.
sentences.zh: 首先，这是联邦政府首次尝试以恐怖主义相关罪名起诉美国抗议者，无论是左翼还是右翼。

sentences.en: And it was also the first time that the government has prosecuted what they call an Antifa cell.
sentences.zh: 这也是政府首次起诉他们所谓的“反法西斯”小组。

sentences.en: Right, because we don't think of Antifa as really having much of an organization at all, let alone having cells.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为我们并不认为“反法西斯”真的有什么组织，更不用说有小组了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: There's no group known as Antifa, right?
sentences.zh: 根本没有一个叫“反法西斯”的组织，对吧？

sentences.en: The term has been used by the GOP as a sort of catch-all for the left.
sentences.zh: 这个词一直被共和党用作左翼的统称。

sentences.en: And as you said, it's not an organization.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它不是一个组织。

sentences.en: It isn't a group with cells the way sort of Al-Qaeda or ISIS or some other foreign terrorist group that we've heard of would have cells.
sentences.zh: 它不像我们听说过的基地组织、伊斯兰国或其他外国恐怖组织那样，拥有严密的小组。

sentences.en: It's a very loose, decentralized movement of left-wing activists whose ideology is kind of broadly anti-fasciSt.
sentences.zh: 它是一个非常松散、去中心化的左翼活动家运动，其意识形态大体上是反法西斯的。

sentences.en: And that's what Antifa stands for.
sentences.zh: 这就是“反法西斯”的含义。

sentences.en: Anti-fasciSt.
sentences.zh: 反法西斯。

sentences.en: Antifa.
sentences.zh: 反法西斯。

sentences.en: And that's what made this prosecution, for me as somebody who's reported on terrorism cases for years, shocking, frankly.
sentences.zh: 作为一个报道恐怖主义案件多年的人，坦率地说，这起起诉让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: Well, we're going to get very deeply into this prosecution and into the government's decision to charge the folks in this case as an Antifa cell.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们将深入探讨这起起诉，以及政府决定将本案中的人员定性为“反法西斯”小组的决定。

sentences.en: But let's just start with the very basics of this case.
sentences.zh: 但让我们先从这起案件的最基本情况开始。

sentences.en: You went and did a lot of independent reporting to try to understand who they are, what motivated them.
sentences.zh: 你进行了大量的独立报道，试图了解他们是谁，是什么激励了他们。

sentences.en: What did you end up finding?
sentences.zh: 你最终发现了什么？

sentences.en: So I spent months looking through documents, talking to a lot of people who knew the protesters and even more people who were just part of the larger left-wing scene.
sentences.zh: 我花了几个月时间查阅文件，采访了许多认识这些抗议者的人，以及更多只是参与了更广泛左翼圈子的人。

sentences.en: And what I came to see very quickly is that the place that this happened in Dallas-Fort Worth
sentences.zh: 我很快发现，这起事件发生的达拉斯-沃斯堡地区，

sentences.en: does not have a sort of established protest scene in the way that, say, a city like Seattle or Portland
sentences.zh: 并没有像西雅图、波特兰，

sentences.en: or New York or some other sort of blue city, frankly, that have, you know, really long histories of progressive activism.
sentences.zh: 或者纽约等其他所谓的“蓝色城市”那样，拥有那种有着悠久进步主义活动历史的成熟抗议氛围。

sentences.en: Dallas-Fort Worth does not have that.
sentences.zh: 达拉斯-沃斯堡没有这种氛围。

sentences.en: Which makes sense because it's Texas.
sentences.zh: 这很合理，因为这是得克萨斯州。

sentences.en: It wouldn't seem to be a hotbed of left-wing activism.
sentences.zh: 它看起来不像是左翼活动的温床。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so what's seen does exist is more of a patchwork of people with different interests or tendencies.
sentences.zh: 所以现有的景象更像是一个由有着不同兴趣或倾向的人组成的拼凑体。

sentences.en: So you have like the self-styled anarchist types, you have artists, you have LGBTQ activists, you have immigration activists, you have, you know,
sentences.zh: 你有自称无政府主义者的人，有艺术家，有LGBTQ活动家，有移民活动家，还有，你知道的，

sentences.en: a really broad cross-section of people who care about a variety of different social issues who are left of center.
sentences.zh: 一群真正广泛的、关心各种社会议题的中间偏左的人。

sentences.en: And so just like many, many people in this world, they connect with people online.
sentences.zh: 就像这个世界上的许多人一样，他们通过网络与他人建立联系。

sentences.en: And so that's where the central meeting place of this community is.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个社区的核心聚会场所。

sentences.en: And how is it that people involved in this online community end up gathering at this detention center?
sentences.zh: 那么，参与这个在线社区的人是如何最终聚集在这个拘留中心的呢？

sentences.en: So the people I spoke to told me that this had really been brewing for a while.
sentences.zh: 我采访的人告诉我，这种情况其实已经酝酿了一段时间。

sentences.en: Texas's conservative government and legislature had been taking a series of actions for several years
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯州的保守派政府和立法机构几年来一直在采取一系列行动，

sentences.en: that were making a lot of liberals, especially liberal activists, very, very fearful.
sentences.zh: 让许多自由派，尤其是自由派活动家，感到非常、非常恐惧。

sentences.en: They were restricting the rights of trans people.
sentences.zh: 他们限制跨性别者的权利。

sentences.en: They were cracking down on abortion.
sentences.zh: 他们严厉打击堕胎。

sentences.en: They were targeting immigrants.
sentences.zh: 他们针对移民。

sentences.en: In all of these areas, they were way in front of a lot of states in this country.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些领域，他们都走在了全国许多州的前面。

sentences.en: In fact, in some cases, they were at the front.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在某些情况下，他们是领头羊。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Texas's governor, Greg Abbott, was so proud of his immigration crackdown.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯州州长格雷格·阿博特对他的移民打击行动感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: For example, he was literally busing people out of state to Democratic.
sentences.zh: 例如，他实际上是在把人从州内用巴士运往民主党控制的地区。

sentences.en: Yeah, he went around federal immigration law to crackdown.
sentences.zh: 是的，他绕过联邦移民法进行打击。

sentences.en: And so that is the backdrop for this pivotal moment that comes in February of 2021,
sentences.zh: 这就是2021年2月那个关键时刻的背景，

sentences.en: when Texas is hit by this massive, massive winter storm.
sentences.zh: 当时得克萨斯州遭遇了一场大规模的冬季风暴。

sentences.en: that plunges the whole state into these, like, literally sub-zero temperatures.
sentences.zh: 这场风暴让整个州陷入了零度以下的严寒。

sentences.en: And about 5 million homes and businesses across the state lost power.
sentences.zh: 全州约500万户家庭和企业断电。

sentences.en: And what the state actually didn't do was warn people.
sentences.zh: 而州政府实际上没有做的是警告民众。

sentences.en: They had a very weak power grid.
sentences.zh: 他们的电网非常脆弱。

sentences.en: They knew it.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这一点。

sentences.en: They had known it for about 10 years.
sentences.zh: 他们已经知道大约10年了。

sentences.en: They had never, ever made an effort to fix it.
sentences.zh: 但他们从来没有做出任何努力去修复它。

sentences.en: And what happened is you had hundreds of people who literally froze to death in their homes.
sentences.zh: 结果就是有数百人直接冻死在家里。

sentences.en: So these activists who are already feeling fearful and already feeling as if the government doesn't care about them or that the government could like try to legislate them out of existence on some level now are connecting the dots and feeling like,
sentences.zh: 所以这些本已感到恐惧的活动家，觉得政府根本不在乎他们，或者政府可能会在某种程度上通过立法让他们无法生存，现在他们把这些点连了起来，感觉，

sentences.en: you know, oh, my God, we are genuinely at a crisis point.
sentences.zh: “天哪，我们真的处于危机时刻。”

sentences.en: We're genuinely at risk.
sentences.zh: 我们真的处于危险之中。

sentences.en: Our government doesn't care if we live or die.
sentences.zh: 我们的政府根本不在乎我们的死活。

sentences.en: This is a very galvanizing moment for the activists across Dallas-Fort Worth,
sentences.zh: 这对达拉斯-沃斯堡的活动家来说是一个非常激励的时刻，

sentences.en: a lot of whom start to realize that they really need to learn survival skills and how to protect themselves in case something like this happens again.
sentences.zh: 其中许多人开始意识到，他们真的需要学习生存技能，以及如果再次发生这种情况，该如何保护自己。

sentences.en: And one avenue available to them was a group called the Socialist Rifle Association.
sentences.zh: 而他们可用的一个途径是一个叫“社会主义步枪协会”（SRA）的组织。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Not a group I have heard of.
sentences.zh: 这不是我听说过的组织。

sentences.en: The SRA is an organization that has cast itself over the years as sort of the progressive alternative to the National Rifle Association.
sentences.zh: SRA是一个多年来将自己定位为“全国步枪协会”（NRA）的进步替代品的组织。

sentences.en: This is a national organization, so it has branches around the country.
sentences.zh: 这是一个全国性组织，所以在全国各地都有分支机构。

sentences.en: But it functioned in Dallas as a meeting place for a lot of people who wanted to get involved,
sentences.zh: 但在达拉斯，它成为了许多想要参与进来的人的聚会场所，

sentences.en: not just in learning how to shoot guns, but in doing things like mutual aid, you know, in doing like a variety of projects that were all reinforcing of a community
sentences.zh: 不仅是学习如何射击，还包括做互助工作，你知道，做各种能够加强社区、

sentences.en: and sort of building community strength and resiliency.
sentences.zh: 建立社区力量和韧性的项目。

sentences.en: So this scattered group of activists starts to find a home in SRA.
sentences.zh: 于是，这群分散的活动家开始在SRA找到了归宿。

sentences.en: Yeah, some of them.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们中的一些人。

sentences.en: They're gravitating to people or groups that will make them feel more in control.
sentences.zh: 他们被那些能让他们感到更有掌控力的人或团体所吸引。

sentences.en: And one of the figures who sort of represents himself that way is a guy named Ben Song, who was a leader of the SRA.
sentences.zh: 其中一个以这种形象自居的人物是一个叫本·宋的人，他是SRA的领导人。

sentences.en: And Ben was a professional activiSt.
sentences.zh: 本是一名职业活动家。

sentences.en: These are the guys that are just everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这些家伙无处不在。

sentences.en: They're at every proteSt.
sentences.zh: 他们出现在每一次抗议活动中。

sentences.en: They're at the front of every proteSt.
sentences.zh: 他们站在每一次抗议活动的最前线。

sentences.en: Ben was a Marine, had been in the Marine Corps, and he'd been involved in the pro-democracy protests in Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 本曾是一名海军陆战队员，曾在海军陆战队服役，还参与过香港的民主抗议活动。

sentences.en: And this was a huge deal within a community of very inexperienced activists to have a guy who had gone to a foreign country
sentences.zh: 对于一个非常缺乏经验的活动家社区来说，有一个去过外国、

sentences.en: and had thrown himself into these very famous and actually quite violent protests.
sentences.zh: 并投身于这些非常著名且实际上相当暴力的抗议活动的人，是一件大事。

sentences.en: And so he had a myth about him.
sentences.zh: 所以他身上有一种神话色彩。

sentences.en: So Ben creates a group of people around him who are all sort of united in this fear that something terrible is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 于是，本在他周围建立了一个群体，他们都因为担心会发生可怕的事情而团结在一起。

sentences.en: And so they need to be prepared.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要做好准备。

sentences.en: They need to know how to defend themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们需要知道如何保护自己。

sentences.en: They need to know how to use a gun.
sentences.zh: 他们需要知道如何使用枪支。

sentences.en: And they need to be a little small cadre, like a little army, right?
sentences.zh: 他们需要成为一个小团体，就像一支小军队，对吧？

sentences.en: They need to be a tribe.
sentences.zh: 他们需要成为一个部落。

sentences.en: And Ben is the unofficial leader of the tribe.
sentences.zh: 而本就是这个部落的非官方领袖。

sentences.en: He is the expert within the tribe.
sentences.zh: 他是部落里的专家。

sentences.en: And they train at the range.
sentences.zh: 他们在靶场训练。

sentences.en: Shooter ready?
sentences.zh: 射手准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 准备好了。

sentences.en: Target one!
sentences.zh: 目标一！

sentences.zh: 他有相当多的AR-15式步枪，会借给或送给没有枪的人。

sentences.en: Six is down!
sentences.zh: 六号目标倒下！

sentences.en: Move!
sentences.zh: 移动！

sentences.zh: 他主动提出免费教他们自卫。

sentences.en: You just practice these at home.
sentences.zh: 你们只要在家里练习这些动作。

sentences.en: You're going to be able to move your weapon administratively
sentences.zh: 你们就能在管理上移动武器，

sentences.en: Strangely, much faster.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，速度快得多。

sentences.en: Engage much faster, much more accurately.
sentences.zh: 交战速度快得多，也更准确。

sentences.en: So all of this is going on for a couple of years, and it winds up building to a head after Donald Trump is elected.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切持续了几年，在唐纳德·特朗普当选后达到了顶峰。

sentences.en: Because at that point, every fear within this community, particularly when it comes to people who are trans or non-binary, and deportation of those who are of Latino origin,
sentences.zh: 因为在那一刻，这个社区内的所有恐惧，特别是对于跨性别者或非二元性别者，以及对拉丁裔移民的驱逐，

sentences.en: those fears are now becoming a reality in their minds.
sentences.zh: 在他们心中，这些恐惧现在正在成为现实。

sentences.en: So what do Ben and this group that he is essentially leading do with these feelings of being under siege now that Donald Trump is reelected?
sentences.zh: 那么，在唐纳德·特朗普连任后，本和他所领导的这个组织，打算如何处理这种被围困的感觉呢？

sentences.en: So Ben has created a signal group for the broader activist community to share their fears and anxieties.
sentences.zh: 本为更广泛的活动人士群体创建了一个Signal群组，让他们分享彼此的恐惧和焦虑。

sentences.en: And by the spring of 2025, we are seeing some big deal protests, anti-ice protests happening in blue cities like L.A., in Portland, in Seattle.
sentences.zh: 到了2025年春天，我们看到了一些重大的抗议活动，在洛杉矶、波特兰、西雅图等民主党执政的城市，爆发了反移民及海关执法局（ICE）的抗议。

sentences.en: And the Dallas activists are sitting there and going, we need to do something like this.
sentences.zh: 达拉斯的活动人士看在眼里，心想：我们也得做点类似的事情。

sentences.en: So what can we do that would be effective?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们能做些什么才有效呢？

sentences.en: and they come up with an idea that they should do some sort of protest outside of an ICE facility.
sentences.zh: 他们想出了一个主意，要在ICE设施外进行某种抗议。

sentences.en: And Prairieland, which is a privately run ICE facility about an hour from Dallas-Fort Worth, becomes the place that they think, well, maybe that would be a good place to go.
sentences.zh: “草原地带”（Prairieland）——一个距离达拉斯-沃斯堡约一小时车程的私营ICE拘留中心，成了他们认为或许是个好去处的地方。

sentences.en: It's called the Prairieland Detention Center.
sentences.zh: 它叫“草原地带拘留中心”。

sentences.en: And Ben and some other activists are on this private signal chat and they're talking about doing a noise protest on the 4th of July,
sentences.zh: 本和其他一些活动人士在那个私密的Signal群聊里，商量着要在7月4日搞一场噪音抗议，

sentences.en: which they think would be the spectacular moment of symbolism, right?
sentences.zh: 他们认为这会是一个极具象征意义的壮观时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: They're going to hold a protest on the day that America celebrates freedom to show solidarity with people who are detained by the government.
sentences.zh: 他们打算在美国庆祝自由的日子里举行抗议，以声援那些被政府拘留的人们。

sentences.en: And their idea is they're going to set off fireworks outside of this ice facility, Prairieland, to remind the detainees that they haven't been forgotten.
sentences.zh: 他们的想法是，在这个ICE设施外燃放烟花，提醒被拘留者他们并没有被遗忘。

sentences.en: At the same time as they're having this conversation, Ben has another idea.
sentences.zh: 就在他们进行这场对话的同时，本又有了另一个主意。

sentences.en: And he will bring that idea up at a gathering that he's holding with about six or seven activists at a house in Dallas
sentences.zh: 他打算在达拉斯一处民宅举行的聚会上提出这个想法，当时有六七名活动人士在场，

sentences.en: where he starts showing them videos and pictures he's pulled off of the Internet of the Prairieland Detention Center.
sentences.zh: 他开始向他们展示他从网上搜集到的关于“草原地带拘留中心”的视频和图片。

sentences.en: And he begins to point out, look at this guard shack.
sentences.zh: 他开始指出：看这个警卫岗亭。

sentences.en: It's not very well manned.
sentences.zh: 人手并不充足。

sentences.en: Look at these video cameras.
sentences.zh: 看这些监控摄像头。

sentences.en: There's not that many of them.
sentences.zh: 数量并不多。

sentences.en: They might not even be operational.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能根本没在运作。

sentences.en: And all of this leads to him saying to the group, this is going to be as easy as it gets.
sentences.zh: 这一切让他对团队说：这将会是再容易不过的事了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: What will be as easy as it gets?
sentences.zh: 什么会是再容易不过的事？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So several people in the group go, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 所以团队里的几个人问：你在说什么呢？

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: And he goes, oh, we're going to take the place and free the detainees.
sentences.zh: 他说：哦，我们要占领那个地方，把被拘留者放出来。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: We're going to take over a federal immigration detention center.
sentences.zh: 我们要接管一个联邦移民拘留中心。

sentences.en: How?
sentences.zh: 怎么做？

sentences.en: What are we going to shoot our way in?
sentences.zh: 我们要一路开火冲进去吗？

sentences.en: Are we going to kill somebody?
sentences.zh: 我们要杀人吗？

sentences.en: And he says, oh, no, no, no, we're going to lay down suppressive fire.
sentences.zh: 他说：哦，不不不，我们要进行火力压制。

sentences.en: It's just suppressive fire.
sentences.zh: 只是火力压制而已。

sentences.en: It's a way to sort of hold them back.
sentences.zh: 这是一种牵制他们的方法。

sentences.en: And he doesn't really explain much more than that, as far as we know.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，他并没有做更多的解释。

sentences.en: And the group is really shocked by this, and they're like, oh, that sounds like a terrible idea.
sentences.zh: 团队对此感到非常震惊，他们说：哦，这听起来是个糟糕透顶的主意。

sentences.en: We don't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们不想那样做。

sentences.en: That's not what we signed up for.
sentences.zh: 那不是我们加入的目的。

sentences.en: That's not what we signed up for.
sentences.zh: 那不是我们加入的目的。

sentences.en: And so the conversation switches to, okay, well, what could we do?
sentences.zh: 于是对话转变为：好吧，那我们能做什么？

sentences.en: And so they return to this idea of the noise proteSt.
sentences.zh: 他们又回到了最初那个噪音抗议的想法。

sentences.en: and they decide, okay, we're just going to do that.
sentences.zh: 他们决定：好吧，我们就做那个。

sentences.en: One person in the group says, so do we still bring our guns?
sentences.zh: 团队里有人问：那我们还要带枪吗？

sentences.en: And Ben says, oh, definitely.
sentences.zh: 本说：哦，当然要带。

sentences.en: With that, the evening ends, and they, you know, go home.
sentences.zh: 就这样，晚上结束了，他们各自回家了。

sentences.en: It's the night of, and they show up at Prairie Land.
sentences.zh: 到了当晚，他们出现在了“草原地带”。

sentences.en: They park about a quarter mile away on this quiet street.
sentences.zh: 他们把车停在约四分之一英里外的一条安静街道上。

sentences.en: They've scoped this out.
sentences.zh: 他们已经踩过点了。

sentences.en: They're very intent on making sure that they're secure and making sure that they're not identifiable.
sentences.zh: 他们非常在意确保自身安全，并确保自己不会被认出来。

sentences.en: They are wearing black.
sentences.zh: 他们穿着黑色的衣服。

sentences.en: They are wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 他们戴着面具。

sentences.en: They have walkie-talkies to communicate with each other.
sentences.zh: 他们用对讲机进行联络。

sentences.en: And they're using aliases, which they always use.
sentences.zh: 而且他们像往常一样，使用了化名。

sentences.en: So the group gets to the intersection where Prairieland is.
sentences.zh: 团队到达了“草原地带”所在的十字路口。

sentences.en: And most of them hang a left.
sentences.zh: 大多数人向左转。

sentences.en: And they head off to this grassy area that is right in front of the window inside the facility where the detainees might be able to come and look.
sentences.zh: 他们前往那片草地，那里正对着设施内的一扇窗户，被拘留者可能在那里往外看。

sentences.en: And they start to set off fireworks.
sentences.zh: 他们开始燃放烟花。

sentences.en: As planned.
sentences.zh: 按计划进行。

sentences.en: As planned.
sentences.zh: 按计划进行。

sentences.en: Just to be very clear, they're approaching this, the vast majority of them, unarmed.
sentences.zh: 需要说明的是，他们绝大多数人接近这里时并没有携带武器。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There are a few important exceptions, however.
sentences.zh: 不过，有几个重要的例外。

sentences.en: And one of them is Ben.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是本。

sentences.en: Ben has brought his favorite AR-15.
sentences.zh: 本带了他最喜欢的AR-15步枪。

sentences.en: And so he stayed a little bit further down, sort of near the guard shack, to keep guard.
sentences.zh: 所以他留在了离警卫岗亭稍远一点的地方，负责警戒。

sentences.en: The rest of the group, they're setting off fireworks.
sentences.zh: 团队的其他人在燃放烟花。

sentences.en: They're shouting, Esperanza, which is hope in Spanish.
sentences.zh: 他们高喊着“Esperanza”，在西班牙语里是“希望”的意思。

sentences.en: And you see at the window, this very long window inside the facility, all these detainees lined up with their faces pressed against the glass.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到设施内那扇很长的窗户边，所有被拘留者都排成一排，脸紧贴着玻璃。

sentences.en: They were obviously invisibly cheered by this.
sentences.zh: 他们显然受到了这种无声的鼓舞。

sentences.en: One person in this group at the fireworks is a guy that nobody knew and starts heading towards the parking lot and has some spray paint in his backpack and starts spray painting the guard shack and some cars and writing like,
sentences.zh: 团队里有一个没人认识的家伙，在放烟花时开始朝停车场走去，他的背包里装着喷漆，开始在警卫岗亭和一些车上喷涂，写着类似……

sentences.en: fuck you, pig, and traitor, and fuck ice, and things like that.
sentences.zh: “去你的，猪猡”、“叛徒”、“去你的ICE”之类的话。

sentences.en: Not part of the plan.
sentences.zh: 这不在计划之内。

sentences.en: Not part of the plan, and it was also something almost everybody was unaware of.
sentences.zh: 这不在计划之内，而且几乎所有人都对此一无所知。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, inside the ICE facility, the security guards are hearing these fireworks, and they're a little bit worried that something might be hitting the building or whatever.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在ICE设施内，保安听到了这些烟花声，他们有点担心是不是有什么东西击中了建筑物之类的。

sentences.en: And so two of them go out to check out what's going on.
sentences.zh: 于是其中两人出去查看情况。

sentences.en: They see these fireworks going off.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了正在燃放的烟花。

sentences.en: One of them walks right up to the activist and says,
sentences.zh: 其中一人径直走到活动人士面前说：

sentences.en: Hey, you know what, you guys, it's time to go.
sentences.zh: 嘿，你们听着，你们该走了。

sentences.en: You're on private property.
sentences.zh: 这是私人领地。

sentences.en: You got to go.
sentences.zh: 你们得离开。

sentences.en: And the group says, okay.
sentences.zh: 团队说：好的。

sentences.en: And they start packing up.
sentences.zh: 他们开始收拾东西。

sentences.en: You know, they've kind of done their thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们已经完成了他们的事。

sentences.en: It's beginning to rain, so no more fireworks are really going to get set off at this point.
sentences.zh: 天开始下雨了，所以此时不会再有烟花被燃放了。

sentences.en: And they take off.
sentences.zh: 他们离开了。

sentences.en: And the security guard who had told the group to leave, she and her partner are starting to walk towards the parking lot because they're hearing some noises.
sentences.zh: 那个叫他们离开的保安，和她的搭档开始往停车场走，因为他们听到了一些动静。

sentences.en: They're hearing some breaking glass.
sentences.zh: 他们听到玻璃破碎的声音。

sentences.en: They're hearing some pop-pop sounding of, like, tires being popped.
sentences.zh: 他们听到轮胎被扎破时发出的“砰砰”声。

sentences.en: And she now realizes, oh, there's some actual vandalism going on.
sentences.zh: 她现在意识到：哦，真的有人在搞破坏。

sentences.en: They see the spray paint.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了喷漆涂鸦。

sentences.en: And she calls the security desk inside ICE and says, you need to call the police.
sentences.zh: 她给ICE内部的保安室打电话说：你们得报警。

sentences.en: So at that point, we have a local police lieutenant named Thomas Gross who answers that call.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，一位名叫托马斯·格罗斯的当地警督接到了电话。

sentences.en: And he shows up in his car alone without a partner and sees all this graffiti.
sentences.zh: 他独自开车赶到现场，没有带搭档，看到了所有的涂鸦。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, somebody, all in black, runs in front of his car.
sentences.zh: 突然，一个全身黑衣的人从他的车前跑过。

sentences.en: He parks his car, gets out.
sentences.zh: 他停下车，走了出来。

sentences.en: He shouts for this guy to stop.
sentences.zh: 他大喊让那个人停下。

sentences.en: And the next thing you know, Ben, who's wearing a green ski mask and has moved towards the parking lot area, begins to shoot.
sentences.zh: 紧接着，戴着绿色滑雪面罩、已经移动到停车场区域的本，开始开枪。

sentences.en: Lieutenant Gross claims that he did not shoot firSt.
sentences.zh: 格罗斯警督声称他并没有先开枪。

sentences.en: But he returned fire, and there's a quick exchange of fire.
sentences.zh: 但他进行了还击，双方发生了短暂的交火。

sentences.en: In that exchange, Gross is shot.
sentences.zh: 在那次交火中，格罗斯中弹了。

sentences.en: So with the shooting of Lieutenant Gross, everything changes.
sentences.zh: 随着格罗斯警督中弹，一切都变了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Ben begins to run away, and another activist, who is also walking away, sees him racing past him and goes, what the fuck did you do?
sentences.zh: 本开始逃跑，另一名也在撤离的活动人士看到他从身边飞奔而过，问道：你他妈干了什么？

sentences.en: And Ben says, oh shit, oh shit, oh shit, oh shit.
sentences.zh: 本说：糟了，糟了，糟了，糟了。

sentences.en: And he just drops his weapon,
sentences.zh: 他丢下武器，

sentences.en: and disappears.
sentences.zh: 消失了。

sentences.en: And within a very short amount of time, all of these law enforcement have arrived on the scene.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，所有的执法人员都赶到了现场。

sentences.en: Right, a cop has been shot, and they want to find everybody who might be involved.
sentences.zh: 没错，一名警察中弹了，他们想找出所有可能涉案的人。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And they start arresting people.
sentences.zh: 他们开始逮捕相关人员。

sentences.en: But Ben evades capture by hiding in the sunflowers, you know, in a field near the Prairieland facility,
sentences.zh: 但本通过躲在“草原地带”设施附近田野里的向日葵丛中逃脱了抓捕，

sentences.en: until about a day or so later, he's spirited away by some friends that he contacted, and he spends the next two weeks kind of on the lam,
sentences.zh: 直到大约一天后，他被联系到的朋友救走，接下来的两周他都在逃亡，

sentences.en: hiding in the home of one friend and then another friend until he's finally arrested.
sentences.zh: 躲在一个又一个朋友的家里，直到最终被捕。

sentences.en: And once this very disparate group who were all there that night where this cop is shot, once they're arrested, what are they charged with?
sentences.zh: 当那天晚上在场的所有这些各不相同的人被捕后，他们被指控了什么罪名？

sentences.en: Initially, they were charged with attempted murder.
sentences.zh: 最初，他们被指控谋杀未遂。

sentences.en: And Texas is a state that takes a pretty aggressive approach and had identified Ben as the shooter.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州采取了相当激进的做法，并将本认定为枪手。

sentences.en: And they identified the rest of them as sort of the supporting cast that made that shooting possible.
sentences.zh: 他们将其他人认定为促成那次枪击事件的“配角”。

sentences.en: And they had identified this group as holding anti-government views because of some materials they found in their backpacks and their cars.
sentences.zh: 他们还根据在背包和车里发现的一些材料，将该组织定性为持有反政府观点。

sentences.en: And so their perspective was this was a planned ambush of law enforcement and everybody is basically charged with attempted murder and this is going to be a conspiracy case.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的观点是，这是一场针对执法人员的有预谋的伏击，每个人基本上都被指控谋杀未遂，这将是一起共谋案件。

sentences.en: And they proceeded with a case that was by many estimations somewhat of an overreaction.
sentences.zh: 他们推进的这起案件，在许多人看来有些反应过度。

sentences.en: but at the same time was pretty standard.
sentences.zh: 但同时，这在当时也相当普遍。

sentences.en: I mean, they were able to use these laws to go after them in a very punitive kind of way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们能够利用这些法律以一种非常惩罚性的方式来对付他们。

sentences.en: But then, not long after this, the conservative activist Charlie Kirk is killed.
sentences.zh: 但就在这之后不久，保守派活动人士查理·柯克被杀了。

sentences.en: And at that point, everything in this case changes.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，这起案件的一切都变了。

sentences.en: Let me tell you something I'm not sure with anybody, but the last message that Charlie Kirk gave to me was he said that we have to dismantle
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你一些我不确定是否对别人说过的事，查理·柯克给我的最后一条信息是，他说我们必须拆除

sentences.en: the radical left organizations in this country that are fomenting violence that was the last
sentences.zh: 这个国家煽动暴力的激进左翼组织，那是他发给我的最后一条

sentences.zh: 信息。我们马上回来。嘿，我是本杰明·普隆，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听

sentences.zh: 特朗普和他的政府成员长期以来一直将这个国家的政治暴力归咎于左翼，而不是右翼。

sentences.en: So Trump and members of his administration have long blamed political violence in this country, not on the right, but on the left.
sentences.zh: 他们将柯克遇刺视为这方面的例证。

sentences.en: And they saw the Kirk assassination as like the example of that.
sentences.zh: 你看，这就是针对一个众所周知的左翼“避雷针”式人物的暴力行为。

sentences.en: Here it is, violence against a person that is widely known to be a sort of lightning rod for the left.

sentences.zh: 第一项指令是他最初在社交媒体上宣布的，然后……

sentences.en: These are anarchists and agitators, professional anarchists and agitators.
sentences.zh: 这些人是无政府主义者和煽动者，职业的无政府主义者和煽动者。

sentences.zh: 他发布了一项行政命令，将“反法西斯运动”（Antifa）定性为恐怖组织。

sentences.en: even though there is no actual legal mechanism to designate Antifa as a terrorist organization
sentences.zh: 尽管目前没有任何实际的法律机制可以将“反法西斯运动”定性为恐怖组织，

sentences.zh: 就像政府将外国团体定性为恐怖组织那样。

sentences.en: So this is kind of a symbolic statement.
sentences.zh: 所以这更像是一种象征性的声明。

sentences.en: A few days after that executive order, Trump sends out another directive that directs law enforcement to aggressively pursue domestic terror investigations
sentences.zh: 在那项行政命令发布几天后，特朗普又发出了另一项指令，指示执法部门积极开展国内恐怖主义调查，

sentences.en: into people who are associated with what was described in this document as anti-Americanism, anti-capitalism, anti-Christianity, and extremism on immigration, race, and gender.
sentences.zh: 针对那些与该文件中所描述的“反美主义、反资本主义、反基督教，以及在移民、种族和性别问题上的极端主义”有关联的人。

sentences.en: And this memo specifically called on prosecutors to seek the highest penalties available, And it also cites anti-fascism as a key source of political violence.
sentences.zh: 这份备忘录特别要求检察官寻求法律允许的最高刑罚，它还将反法西斯主义列为政治暴力的关键来源。

sentences.en: So what this means is that the Charlie Kirk assassination has unleashed a kind of revenge campaign on the left,
sentences.zh: 这意味着柯克遇刺事件在左翼引发了一场报复运动，

sentences.en: by which the government has directed law enforcement to invest a tremendous amount of its resources into going after people who hold these kinds of views
sentences.zh: 政府指示执法部门投入大量资源去追查那些持有此类观点的人，

sentences.en: and to punish them to the highest extent of the law.
sentences.zh: 并依法对他们进行最严厉的惩处。

sentences.en: Okay, once the president issues these back-to-back directives and there's this new framework for thinking about the threat of left-wing activism,
sentences.zh: 好的，一旦总统发布了这些接连不断的指令，并且有了一个关于左翼激进主义威胁的新思维框架，

sentences.en: what ends up being the impact on this Prairie Land case?
sentences.zh: 这对“草原土地案”（Prairie Land case）最终产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: So the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，美国联邦检察官，

sentences.en: attorney, she was an acting U.S.
sentences.zh: 她当时是达拉斯的代理联邦检察官，

sentences.en: attorney in Dallas, her name is Nancy Larson, had for a long time since she'd been appointed in the spring of that year, in fact, been looking to please the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 名叫南希·拉尔森（Nancy Larson），事实上，自那年春天被任命以来，她一直急于讨好特朗普政府。

sentences.en: This is according to former prosecutors.
sentences.zh: 这是根据前检察官们的说法。

sentences.en: And she saw this opportunity.
sentences.zh: 她看到了这个机会。

sentences.en: She has a case involving the shooting of a law enforcement officer, the defacing of a federal building, and individuals who are charged who
sentences.zh: 她手头有一个案子，涉及枪击执法人员、损毁联邦建筑，以及被指控的个人，他们

sentences.en: believe in an anti-government, anti-law enforcement, anti-Donald Trump ideology.
sentences.zh: 信仰一种反政府、反执法、反唐纳德·特朗普的意识形态。

sentences.en: She also has in her hand a directive from the Justice Department instructing U.S.
sentences.zh: 她手里还有一份来自司法部的指令，指示美国联邦检察官

sentences.en: attorneys to charge every case in the highest, most serious way possible.
sentences.zh: 以最严厉、最严重的方式对每起案件提起诉讼。

sentences.en: So with these two things in mind, she decides to charge them with material support for terrorism.
sentences.zh: 因此，考虑到这两点，她决定以“为恐怖主义提供物质支持”的罪名起诉他们。

sentences.en: So material support is a terrorism law that's been on the books since the 90s.
sentences.zh: “物质支持”是一项自90年代起就已存在的恐怖主义法律。

sentences.en: It became a sort of a go-to for prosecutors who are looking to make cases against supporters of al-Qaeda or Hamas or any other foreign terrorist groups because it could be used against a very broad range of activities.
sentences.zh: 它成了检察官们针对基地组织、哈马斯或其他外国恐怖组织支持者提起诉讼时的“首选”，因为它适用于极其广泛的活动。

sentences.en: When it is used in a domestic context, which it has been, it's usually used to go after people who have arguably provided support for what we would all think is terror,
sentences.zh: 当它被用于国内环境时——这种情况确实发生过——通常是用来对付那些被认为提供了我们大家所认为的恐怖活动支持的人，

sentences.en: like blowing up infrastructure or providing the material to damage the power grid or something like that.
sentences.zh: 比如炸毁基础设施，或者提供破坏电网的材料之类的。

sentences.en: And that's not uncommon.
sentences.zh: 这并不罕见。

sentences.en: What is uncommon is that it's never used against protesters.
sentences.zh: 罕见的是，它从未被用于抗议者。

sentences.en: And the DOJ has made a really big point of avoiding that.
sentences.zh: 司法部一直非常刻意地避免这样做。

sentences.en: It's very close to treading on speech, treading on the First Amendment.
sentences.zh: 这非常接近于侵犯言论自由，侵犯宪法第一修正案。

sentences.en: And so to use it is kind of the nuclear option.
sentences.zh: 所以使用它就像是动用了“核选项”。

sentences.en: But Nancy Larson decided to go for it.
sentences.zh: 但南希·拉尔森决定孤注一掷。

sentences.en: So how does Nancy Larson use this statute that is generally focused on foreign terrorists on domestic protesters?
sentences.zh: 那么，南希·拉尔森是如何将这项通常针对外国恐怖分子的法规用到国内抗议者身上的呢？

sentences.en: So there's a part of the law that allows prosecutors to go after individuals for what they call terrorist acts.
sentences.zh: 法律中有一部分允许检察官以所谓的“恐怖主义行为”为由追究个人责任。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing about the way they charge these people and the reason that they use this particular law was because this part of the law does
sentences.zh: 关于他们指控这些人的方式，以及他们使用这项特定法律的原因，有趣之处在于法律的这一部分

sentences.en: not require you to be a member of a terrorist group to think of yourself as committing any
sentences.zh: 并不要求你必须是恐怖组织的成员才会被认为犯下了任何

sentences.en: act of terrorism, all it requires is that you committed one of the crimes that the government says can be terrorism.
sentences.zh: 恐怖主义行为，它唯一的要求是你犯下了政府所说的可能构成恐怖主义的罪行之一。

sentences.en: And there are about 50 or so crimes, federal crimes, that could qualify as a terrorist act.
sentences.zh: 大约有50种左右的联邦罪行可以被定性为恐怖主义行为。

sentences.en: And ultimately, Larson determined that there were three crimes that would allow her to charge these people with material support for terrorism.
sentences.zh: 最终，拉尔森认定有三项罪行可以让她以“为恐怖主义提供物质支持”的罪名起诉这些人。

sentences.en: So one of them was defacing government property, which was vandalism.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是损毁政府财产，也就是蓄意破坏。

sentences.en: The other one was setting off fireworks that qualified as explosives and the attempted murder of federal law enforcement or someone coming to the aid of federal law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 另一个是燃放被认定为爆炸物的烟花，以及谋杀联邦执法人员或协助联邦执法人员的人未遂。

sentences.en: The ICE facility was manned by people on contract to the federal government, so they qualified as some form of federal law enforcement, and
sentences.zh: 那个移民及海关执法局（ICE）设施由受雇于联邦政府的人员把守，因此他们被视为某种形式的联邦执法人员，而

sentences.en: Lieutenant Gross was coming to their aid.
sentences.zh: 格罗斯中尉（Lieutenant Gross）当时正赶去支援他们。

sentences.en: So the shooting of him qualified as the attempted murder that could qualify as a terrorist act.
sentences.zh: 所以枪击他被定性为谋杀未遂，从而可以被定性为恐怖主义行为。

sentences.en: So once this prosecutor breaks all kinds of norms and files these charges in a way that the Department of Justice has long avoided,
sentences.zh: 那么，当这位检察官打破各种常规，以司法部长期避免的方式提起这些指控后，

sentences.en: what happens once those charges actually reach the courtroom?
sentences.zh: 这些指控一旦进入法庭会发生什么？

sentences.en: So in February, I went to Fort Worth to attend the trial of these.
sentences.zh: 二月份，我去了沃斯堡参加他们的审判。

sentences.en: At this point, it was nine activists.
sentences.zh: 当时有九名活动人士。

sentences.en: And it's important to know that it was prosecuted in Fort Worth because Fort Worth is very conservative.
sentences.zh: 需要注意的是，审判是在沃斯堡进行的，因为沃斯堡非常保守。

sentences.en: And the two judges in the Fort Worth federal courthouse are very conservative.
sentences.zh: 沃斯堡联邦法院的两名法官也非常保守。

sentences.en: When the case opened, so the onus is on the government to prove that these people did what they accused them of doing,
sentences.zh: 案件开庭时，政府有责任证明这些人确实做了他们被指控的事情，

sentences.en: which is not just vandalizing a building or shooting at a police officer but doing that for a political purpose.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是破坏建筑物或向警察开枪，而是为了政治目的而这样做。

sentences.en: That's what would make it terrorism, right?
sentences.zh: 这才是使其成为恐怖主义的原因，对吧？

sentences.en: And so in order to do that, they must bring in their ideology which under law you cannot prosecute a person for
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，他们必须引入他们的意识形态，虽然法律规定你不能因为一个人的意识形态而起诉他，

sentences.en: but you can bring an ideology if it informs the motive or the intent.
sentences.zh: 但如果意识形态能说明动机或意图，你就可以将其引入。

sentences.en: So the prosecution opens their case with sort of a spectacular story of an Antifa cell that met on Signal, an encrypted chat platform,
sentences.zh: 于是，检方以一个引人注目的故事开场，讲述了一个在加密聊天平台Signal上会面的“反法西斯运动”小组，

sentences.en: to discuss their plans to attack this facility.
sentences.zh: 讨论他们攻击该设施的计划。

sentences.en: And they bring out all the things that they consider the evidence in this case.
sentences.zh: 他们拿出了所有他们认为的本案证据。

sentences.en: So they bring out chat transcripts where they discuss the protest and the planning.
sentences.zh: 他们拿出了讨论抗议和策划的聊天记录。

sentences.en: They bring out into the courtroom all these guns, all these AR-15s, and photographs of weapons.
sentences.zh: 他们把所有的枪支、所有的AR-15步枪和武器照片带进了法庭。

sentences.en: And they bring in the fact that Ben Song and a number of the other activists were members of the SRA, the Socialist Rifle Association.
sentences.zh: 他们还提出了本·宋（Ben Song）和其他几名活动人士是“社会主义步枪协会”（SRA）成员的事实。

sentences.en: Some were members of the John Brown Gun Club, which is a much more militant kind of organization.
sentences.zh: 有些人是“约翰·布朗枪支俱乐部”的成员，那是一个更激进的组织。

sentences.en: And they bring in the fact that they had all these zines and flyers and books.
sentences.zh: 他们还带进来了他们拥有的所有杂志、传单和书籍。

sentences.en: And one of the most important parts of this case was that a number of the activists were involved in an anarchist book group called the Emma Goldman Book Club,
sentences.zh: 本案最重要的部分之一是，一些活动人士参与了一个名为“艾玛·戈德曼读书俱乐部”的无政府主义读书小组，

sentences.en: which was exactly what it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 这正如其名。

sentences.en: It was a book club.
sentences.zh: 它就是一个读书俱乐部。

sentences.en: And yet, the government considered the Emma Goldman Book Club to be the recruiting ground for the Antifa cell.
sentences.zh: 然而，政府却认为“艾玛·戈德曼读书俱乐部”是“反法西斯运动”小组的招募基地。

sentences.en: So the prosecution is connecting a lot of dots here.
sentences.zh: 所以检方在这里把很多点连在了一起。

sentences.en: And they say, in our view, this is terrorism and this is Antifa.
sentences.zh: 他们说，在我们看来，这就是恐怖主义，这就是“反法西斯运动”。

sentences.en: But I have the question of why so far in our conversation and the way you've talked about this group of protesters and what motivated them, why you never mentioned the word Antifa?
sentences.zh: 但我有个疑问，为什么在我们至今的谈话中，以及你谈论这群抗议者及其动机的方式中，你从未提到过“反法西斯运动”这个词？

sentences.en: So was there any actual connection between these activists and that idea, that acronym?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些活动人士与那个理念、那个缩写之间真的有任何实际联系吗？

sentences.en: A question was put to five activists who pled guilty and were cooperators and testified about Antifa.
sentences.zh: 有人向五名认罪并配合调查、就“反法西斯运动”作证的活动人士提出了这个问题。

sentences.en: Not one of them denied that they held anti-fascist views.
sentences.zh: 他们中没有一个人否认自己持有反法西斯观点。

sentences.en: And in fact, some of them said, isn't it a good thing to be anti-fascist, right?
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中一些人说，反法西斯难道不是件好事吗？

sentences.en: Don't we all hate fascism?
sentences.zh: 难道我们不都痛恨法西斯主义吗？

sentences.en: None of them, however, identified as Antifa in a sort of organized group way.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们中没有人以某种有组织团体的形式认同自己是“反法西斯运动”成员。

sentences.en: And we've already discussed how Antifa—
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论过“反法西斯运动”是如何——

sentences.en: Isn't really an organized group.
sentences.zh: 并不是一个真正的有组织团体。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so on one of the last days of the trial, they call to the stand a guy who's been sitting in the courtroom for three weeks named Kyle Scheidler.
sentences.zh: 所以在审判的最后几天，他们传唤了一名已经在法庭上坐了三周的人上台作证，他叫凯尔·谢德勒（Kyle Scheidler）。

sentences.en: He is a little-known figure in the world of counterterrorism, but is a well-known figure on the right as being an expert on the Muslim Brotherhood and most recently on Antifa.
sentences.zh: 他在反恐领域是个鲜为人知的人物，但在右翼圈子里却很有名，被视为穆斯林兄弟会，以及最近被视为“反法西斯运动”的专家。

sentences.en: He's very fixated on Antifa.
sentences.zh: 他非常痴迷于“反法西斯运动”。

sentences.en: And in September of 2025, right around the time that Kirk was killed, he published an essay in a right-wing magazine called How to Dismantle Far-Left Extremist Networks.
sentences.zh: 2025年9月，就在柯克遇刺前后，他在一本右翼杂志上发表了一篇题为《如何瓦解极左极端网络》的文章。

sentences.en: And he described that as a roadmap for countering radical left ideologies and organizations.
sentences.zh: 他将其描述为对抗激进左翼意识形态和组织的路线图。

sentences.en: Among the roadmap recommendations was for the Justice Department to bring seditious conspiracy and material support for terrorism charges.
sentences.zh: 路线图中的建议之一是让司法部提起煽动性共谋和为恐怖主义提供物质支持的指控。

sentences.en: Which is what happens.
sentences.zh: 而这正是后来发生的事情。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Kyle Scheidler...
sentences.zh: 凯尔·谢德勒……

sentences.en: Creates the template for the prosecution and then testifies for the prosecution.
sentences.zh: 为检方创建了模板，然后又为检方作证。

sentences.en: And not only that, he created the definition of Antifa that the prosecution used in its indictment and used in the trial.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他还创造了检方在起诉书和审判中使用的“反法西斯运动”的定义。

sentences.en: I mean, this is highly unusual for any civilian, non-DOJ employee, non-lawyer, to be consulting with the prosecutors on any wording of a federal terrorism indictment,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对于任何平民、非司法部雇员、非律师来说，与检察官商讨联邦恐怖主义起诉书的措辞是非常罕见的，

sentences.en: any of the wording.
sentences.zh: 任何措辞都是如此。

sentences.en: So Scheidler is asked to essentially identify what Antifa is and what would be behavior that's Antifa-like.
sentences.zh: 所以谢德勒基本上被要求界定什么是“反法西斯运动”，以及什么样的行为是“反法西斯运动”式的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he testifies that wearing black block, which is, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以他作证说，穿着“黑块”（Black Bloc），也就是，你知道的，

sentences.en: the black clothing and the black mask is both Antifa-like behavior and possibly could be connected to a potentially violent intent.
sentences.zh: 黑色的衣服和黑色的面罩，既是“反法西斯运动”式的行为，也可能与潜在的暴力意图有关。

sentences.en: He testifies about the use of walkie-talkies.
sentences.zh: 他作证提到了对对讲机的使用。

sentences.en: He testifies about the use of aliases.
sentences.zh: 他作证提到了对化名的使用。

sentences.en: At one point, a point is made that none of these people in their signal chats ever talked about violence at all in any capacity.
sentences.zh: 有一次，有人指出这些人在Signal聊天中从未以任何方式谈论过暴力。

sentences.en: And he says, well, of course not, because that would be a violation of security culture.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，当然不会，因为那会违反安全文化。

sentences.en: Of course they would never do this.
sentences.zh: 当然他们永远不会这样做。

sentences.en: Because we can't prove that you're a terrorist, that means that you're a terrorist has been used over and over again.
sentences.zh: 因为“我们无法证明你是恐怖分子，这意味着你是恐怖分子”这种逻辑被反复使用。

sentences.en: It's a circular logic.
sentences.zh: 这是一种循环论证。

sentences.en: It's a very circular logic.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常循环的逻辑。

sentences.en: So when Scheidler was done, the government more or less rested its case.
sentences.zh: 所以当谢德勒作证结束后，政府基本上就完成了举证。

sentences.en: So how does the defense respond to this?
sentences.zh: 那么辩方对此有何回应？

sentences.en: What argument does it put forward on behalf of the folks who are outside this detention center?
sentences.zh: 他们为那些在拘留中心外的人提出了什么论点？

sentences.en: So the defense has been challenging the prosecution's argument every step of the way.
sentences.zh: 辩方在每一个环节都在挑战检方的论点。

sentences.en: Their argument is that this was a peaceful protest that went wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们的论点是，这是一场和平抗议，但出了岔子。

sentences.en: And so throughout the trial, in cross-examination, in their responses, they're constantly challenging this narrative and saying, I'm sorry,
sentences.zh: 所以在整个审判过程中，在交叉询问中，在他们的回应中，他们不断挑战这种叙事，并说，抱歉，

sentences.en: but what you're saying here does not amount to what you said.
sentences.zh: 你在这里所说的并不等同于你之前所说的。

sentences.en: It's just you're not proving your case.
sentences.zh: 这只是你没能证明你的案子。

sentences.en: So when the prosecution rests, the defense rests.
sentences.zh: 所以当检方结束举证时，辩方也结束了举证。

sentences.en: Was the defense right to think that they didn't need to put on much of a case because the prosecution had failed to persuasively make its case?
sentences.zh: 辩方认为他们不需要进行太多辩护，因为检方未能令人信服地完成举证，这种想法对吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不对。

sentences.en: They were wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们错了。

sentences.en: They were wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们错了。

sentences.en: And it took about two days for the jury to find every single one of those defendants guilty.
sentences.zh: 陪审团花了大约两天时间就判定所有被告有罪。

sentences.en: They weren't all guilty of attempted murder.
sentences.zh: 他们并非都犯有谋杀未遂罪。

sentences.en: Only Ben was found guilty of attempted murder.
sentences.zh: 只有本被判谋杀未遂罪成立。

sentences.en: But they were all found guilty of material support for terror.
sentences.zh: 但他们都被判为恐怖主义提供物质支持罪成立。

sentences.en: The most provocative, the most unusual of the charges.
sentences.zh: 这是所有指控中最具挑衅性、最不寻常的一项。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And two months after this, they are sentenced.
sentences.zh: 两个月后，他们被判刑了。

sentences.en: And the sentences were astonishing.
sentences.zh: 判决结果令人震惊。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, let's start with a man who wasn't even at the scene that night.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们从那个那天晚上甚至不在现场的人说起。

sentences.en: His name is Daniel Sanchez Estrada.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫丹尼尔·桑切斯·埃斯特拉达（Daniel Sanchez Estrada）。
zh_words: 丹尼尔·桑切斯·埃斯特拉达

sentences.en: He's the husband of one of the Prairieland protesters.
sentences.zh: 他是其中一名“草原土地”抗议者的丈夫。

sentences.en: And he was charged and convicted of concealing documents and with his wife conspiring to conceal documents, which turned out to be a box of leftist pamphlets and other material
sentences.zh: 他被指控并被判犯有隐匿文件罪，并与其妻子共谋隐匿文件，结果发现那是一箱左翼小册子和其他材料，

sentences.en: the police found in the trunk of his car.
sentences.zh: 警察在他汽车后备箱里发现的。

sentences.en: He was sentenced to 30 years.
sentences.zh: 他被判处30年监禁。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: His wife, who was one of the people who planned the protest and was the sort of driver of wanting to do a noise proteSt.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子，是策划抗议活动的人之一，也是想要进行噪音抗议的推动者。

sentences.en: She's a poet.
sentences.zh: 她是一位诗人。

sentences.en: She's a doula.
sentences.zh: 她是一位导乐（分娩助手）。

sentences.en: And she was the one that shouted Esperanza.
sentences.zh: 她就是那个高喊“埃斯佩兰萨”（Esperanza）的人。

sentences.en: She got 70 years.
sentences.zh: 她被判了70年。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Why 70 years?
sentences.zh: 为什么是70年？

sentences.en: Ostensibly because—
sentences.zh: 表面上是因为——

sentences.en: No arms, no violence.
sentences.zh: 没有武器，没有暴力。

sentences.en: Not only no arms, no violence.
sentences.zh: 不仅没有武器，也没有暴力。

sentences.en: She vocally opposed guns.
sentences.zh: 她公开反对枪支。

sentences.en: She was the one that said, I don't know about guns.
sentences.zh: 正是她说：“我不确定枪支的事。”

sentences.en: That could make the situation more hot.
sentences.zh: 那可能会让局势变得更紧张。

sentences.en: But she was heavily involved in planning this proteSt.
sentences.zh: 但她深度参与了这次抗议活动的策划。

sentences.en: And so the planning is what made her a potential terroriSt.
sentences.zh: 所以正是这种策划行为让她成为了潜在的恐怖分子。

sentences.en: And the other sentences were just as harsh.
sentences.zh: 其他人的判决也同样严厉。

sentences.en: Most of the others in the group got 50 years.
sentences.zh: 小组中大多数人都被判了50年。

sentences.en: Can you just put these sentences into some perspective for me?
sentences.zh: 你能帮我把这些判决放在一个背景中审视一下吗？

sentences.en: Interestingly enough, most people who are prosecuted for material support for terrorism in this country receive under 10 years.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，在这个国家，大多数因向恐怖主义提供物质支持而被起诉的人，刑期都在10年以下。

sentences.en: I mean, these are the kinds of sentences that you would get if you were the leader of a drug cartel, that you would get if you were a member of the mafia.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些刑期通常是贩毒集团头目或黑手党成员才会得到的。

sentences.en: High level.
sentences.zh: 高层。

sentences.en: These are high level leaders of drug cartels or mafioses.
sentences.zh: 那是贩毒集团或黑手党的高层头目。

sentences.en: Responsible for untold numbers of deaths.
sentences.zh: 他们对无数人的死亡负责。

sentences.en: Untold numbers of deaths, for extreme, extreme violence.
sentences.zh: 对无数人的死亡负责，对极端、极端的暴力负责。

sentences.en: And no one was killed here.
sentences.zh: 而这里没有人死亡。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: No one was killed.
sentences.zh: 没有人死亡。

sentences.en: And I should say that Ben Song, who shot at Lieutenant Gross, was given a sentence of 100 years.
sentences.zh: 我还要说，向格罗斯中尉开枪的本·宋被判了100年。

sentences.en: And Lieutenant Gross's injury was relatively minor.
sentences.zh: 而格罗斯中尉的伤势相对较轻。

sentences.en: He was not hospitalized.
sentences.zh: 他没有住院。

sentences.en: He went to the hospital, was treated, and was released in about an hour.
sentences.zh: 他去了医院，接受了治疗，大约一小时后就出院了。

sentences.en: So how integral was the charge of material support for terrorism to the astonishing length of these sentences?
sentences.zh: 那么，“向恐怖主义提供物质支持”这一指控，对这些惊人的刑期有多大的决定性作用？

sentences.en: It certainly enhanced the length of the sentences.
sentences.zh: 它确实加重了刑期。

sentences.en: But I think what was integral to these sentences was the belief system.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这些判决的核心在于信仰体系。

sentences.en: Because even though the prosecution could not prosecute them for their ideology and could only bring in their ideology to suggest their intent,
sentences.zh: 因为尽管检方不能因他们的意识形态起诉他们，只能用意识形态来暗示他们的意图，

sentences.en: the judge who sentenced them could use the ideology to impose these extremely long sentences.
sentences.zh: 但判刑的法官却可以利用这种意识形态来施加这些极长的刑期。

sentences.en: And one of the judges, in fact, reportedly said during sentencing that he was imposing these sentences as a deterrent to other people who might share this ideology.
sentences.zh: 事实上，据报道，其中一位法官在判刑时说，他做出这些判决是为了震慑其他可能持有这种意识形态的人。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Janet, how should we think about this case and its outcome?
sentences.zh: 珍妮特，我们该如何看待这个案件及其结果？

sentences.en: Should we think of it as an outlier because it was the first of its kind, because every element of it seems so specific,
sentences.zh: 我们应该把它看作一个特例，因为它在同类案件中是首例，而且它的每一个要素看起来都非常具体，

sentences.en: including the fact that it was tried in a very conservative part of the country where I have to imagine the jury may not have been particularly sympathetic to the defendants?
sentences.zh: 包括它是在这个国家一个非常保守的地区审理的，我不得不认为陪审团可能对被告并不怎么同情？

sentences.en: Or should we view it as a really important template for how the government starts to treat protests and ideologies that it doesn't like as terrorism?
sentences.zh: 还是我们应该把它看作一个非常重要的模板，即政府开始将它不喜欢的抗议和意识形态视为恐怖主义？

sentences.en: I don't even think this was an unsympathetic jury.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是一个缺乏同情心的陪审团。

sentences.en: There were jurors who argued vocally in the jury room to the point where people heard them, having very spirited debates about this case.
sentences.zh: 陪审团室里有陪审员大声争论，甚至到了外面都能听到的程度，他们对这个案件进行了非常激烈的辩论。

sentences.en: When they came in to deliver their verdict, I think at least one of the jurors had been crying and seemed very distraught.
sentences.zh: 当他们进来宣读判决时，我想至少有一名陪审员一直在哭，看起来非常痛苦。

sentences.en: But once they were confronted with these undisputable facts, they were really in a bind because the government had essentially said to them,
sentences.zh: 但一旦面对这些无可辩驳的事实，他们真的陷入了困境，因为政府本质上已经对他们说，

sentences.en: these facts make these people terrorists.
sentences.zh: 这些事实证明这些人就是恐怖分子。

sentences.en: So in a sense, once these charges were brought, this jury was boxed in.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，一旦这些指控被提出，陪审团就被困住了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: In this case, one of those acts of terror was vandalism.
sentences.zh: 在这个案件中，其中一种恐怖行为是蓄意破坏。

sentences.en: vandalism under many, many, many, many other circumstances is simply vandalism.
sentences.zh: 在许多、许多、许多、许多其他情况下，蓄意破坏仅仅就是蓄意破坏。

sentences.en: And so that was the bind that the jury found themselves in.
sentences.zh: 这就是陪审团发现自己陷入的困境。

sentences.en: They were looking at crimes that were fairly minimal aside from the shooting of a police officer.
sentences.zh: 除了枪击警察之外，他们所审视的罪行相当轻微。

sentences.en: But when it becomes an act of terror, now you're in a different category.
sentences.zh: 但当它变成恐怖行为时，你就进入了另一个范畴。

sentences.en: And so that's how you find a group of activists, most of whom don't have criminal records of any sort going to prison for 30, 40, 50, 70, 100 years.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你会发现一群大多数没有任何犯罪记录的活动人士，被判入狱30、40、50、70、100年。

sentences.en: And that outcome feels totally inextricably linked to the Trump administration's decision to articulate this idea that left-wing activism and activists should be seen as terrorism.
sentences.zh: 这种结果感觉与特朗普政府决定阐述“左翼激进主义和活动人士应被视为恐怖主义”这一理念有着不可分割的联系。

sentences.en: I'm just thinking back to that original executive order that you mentioned much earlier in our conversation where the president was ticking through all the forms of activism that he wanted to treat as domestic terrorism.
sentences.zh: 我回想起你在我们谈话早期提到的那项最初的行政命令，总统列举了他想要当作国内恐怖主义来对待的所有形式的激进主义。

sentences.en: And they're all viewpoints that he disagrees with.
sentences.zh: 而这些都是他不同意的观点。

sentences.en: Anti-capitalism, anti-Christianity, extremism on immigration.
sentences.zh: 反资本主义、反基督教、移民问题上的极端主义。

sentences.en: And that inevitably raises the question, if the president right now wants to, in a certain sense, criminalize protest that he doesn't like,
sentences.zh: 这不可避免地引出了一个问题：如果现在的总统在某种意义上想要将他不喜欢的抗议活动定为犯罪，

sentences.en: which happens in this moment to be left-wing activism, who's to say that the next president won't criminalize the activism of the right or the middle?
sentences.zh: 而目前碰巧是左翼激进主义，谁能说下一任总统不会将右翼或中间派的激进主义定为犯罪呢？

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: I mean, how much is that a real risk?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有多大的现实风险？

sentences.en: That's a real risk.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正的风险。

sentences.en: I think that's a real risk.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个真正的风险。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that there's, so there's a line that prosecutors use, bad facts make bad law.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，检察官有一句口头禅：糟糕的事实会导致糟糕的法律。

sentences.en: And what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: So what that means is that you have a fact in your case that makes your case, if you're a defense attorney, kind of losable, right?
sentences.zh: 意思是，如果你是辩护律师，你的案件中有一个事实让你几乎必输无疑，对吧？

sentences.en: You have a fact that looks bad.
sentences.zh: 你有一个看起来很糟糕的事实。

sentences.en: In this case, it was the shooting of a police officer.
sentences.zh: 在这个案件中，就是枪击警察。

sentences.en: You cannot minimize that a police officer was shot.
sentences.zh: 你无法淡化警察被枪击的事实。

sentences.en: Once you did that, that opens up a huge can of worMs.
sentences.zh: 一旦你做了这件事，就打开了一个巨大的潘多拉魔盒。

sentences.en: And that's the thing that initiates this permission structure without the shooting of the police officer.
sentences.zh: 如果没有枪击警察这件事，这就是启动这种许可结构的因素。

sentences.en: I'm not sure these guys would have gotten prosecuted.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这些人会被起诉。

sentences.en: Maybe not at all, but certainly not in the way that they were.
sentences.zh: 也许根本不会，但肯定不会以他们现在这种方式被起诉。

sentences.en: But with the shooting of the police officer, where you have an undisputed act of violence, that allowed the government to basically say, well, see, they are terrorists.
sentences.zh: 但随着枪击警察事件的发生，当你有一个无可争议的暴力行为时，这让政府基本上可以说：看，他们就是恐怖分子。

sentences.en: See, they are violent.
sentences.zh: 看，他们是暴力的。

sentences.en: Here's political violence.
sentences.zh: 这就是政治暴力。

sentences.en: Let's charge them all as violent terrorists.
sentences.zh: 让我们把他们都指控为暴力恐怖分子。

sentences.en: And where that makes bad law is that if it is not somehow overturned in an appeals court, which at the moment it's very uncertain what will happen,
sentences.zh: 而这之所以会产生糟糕的法律，是因为如果它不能在上诉法院以某种方式被推翻——目前还不确定会发生什么——

sentences.en: that bad law can be applied to anybody.
sentences.zh: 那种糟糕的法律就可以适用于任何人。

sentences.en: So as long as you've created a permission structure to go after people that you disagree with based on your belief that their ideology is dangerous,
sentences.zh: 所以，只要你创造了一种许可结构，可以基于你认为对方意识形态危险的信念去对付你不同意的人，

sentences.en: then anybody can use that same template to go after a different group of people.
sentences.zh: 那么任何人都可以使用同样的模板去对付另一群人。

sentences.en: So, while this was used against the left, four years or five years from now, it could easily be used against the right.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然这被用来对付左翼，但四五年后，它很容易被用来对付右翼。

sentences.en: This is the kind of case that January 6th, arguably, based on everything that occurred, could easily be called a terrorist incident.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种案件，可以说，基于所发生的一切，1月6日事件很容易被称为恐怖主义事件。

sentences.en: There were a million things that people did on January 6th that qualified, but they weren't charged in that matter.
sentences.zh: 人们在1月6日做了无数符合条件的事情，但他们并没有被那样指控。

sentences.en: And then they actually walked out of prison after a very short amount of time.
sentences.zh: 而且他们实际上在很短的时间后就走出了监狱。

sentences.en: But if there's something similar like that happened in another administration, they could go after all of them and make it a serious,
sentences.zh: 但如果另一届政府发生了类似的事情，他们可以去追究所有人的责任，并使之成为一个严重的、

sentences.en: serious situation where people would be sentenced to 40, 50, 60 years.
sentences.zh: 严重的情况，人们会被判处40、50、60年监禁。

sentences.en: Right, and suddenly we have a system from the top on down, the president on down, where terrorism is in the eye of the beholder.
sentences.zh: 没错，突然之间，我们从上到下，从总统到基层，拥有了一个系统，其中恐怖主义完全取决于旁观者的眼光。

sentences.en: And that is not something we've ever had.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是我们曾经有过的。

sentences.en: That's not a tradition we have legally in this country.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们在法律上所拥有的传统。

sentences.en: Terrorism is supposed to be terrorism.
sentences.zh: 恐怖主义理应就是恐怖主义。

sentences.en: The idea that terrorism is in the eye of the beholder is the danger in declaring a war on terror.
sentences.zh: “恐怖主义取决于旁观者的眼光”这一观点，正是宣布反恐战争的危险所在。

sentences.en: As somebody who's been reporting on it for a long time, this is why anyone who has been involved in prosecuting terrorism, in working in law enforcement, they understand that.
sentences.zh: 作为一名长期报道此事的记者，这就是为什么任何参与过起诉恐怖主义、在执法部门工作过的人，他们都明白这一点。

sentences.en: That once you declare a war on terror, which is actually a war on fear in a lot of ways, right, weaponizing that, you're weaponizing your fear,
sentences.zh: 一旦你宣布反恐战争——在很多方面实际上是针对恐惧的战争，对吧——将其武器化，你就是在武器化你的恐惧，

sentences.en: you're weaponizing your dehumanization of your enemy.
sentences.zh: 你就是在武器化你对敌人的非人化。

sentences.en: When you can do that, that cannot be stopped.
sentences.zh: 当你能做到这一点时，它是无法停止的。

sentences.en: That could mean you're a radical supporter or what somebody says is a radical supporter of literally anything, as long as you can find the construct to brand it as terrorism.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你可能是任何事物的激进支持者，或者别人所说的激进支持者，只要你能找到将其贴上恐怖主义标签的结构。

sentences.en: And that's what we did with Prairieland.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们对“草原地带”所做的事情。

sentences.en: And I think this is a dangerous corner that we've turned in this case.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这个案件中，我们转入了一个危险的角落。

sentences.en: Well, Janet, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，珍妮特，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 感激不尽。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: On Monday, the artificial intelligence giant Anthropic offered the most detailed look inside its finances to date when it filed paperwork to soon become a publicly traded company.
sentences.zh: 周一，人工智能巨头Anthropic在提交即将成为上市公司的文件时，提供了迄今为止对其财务状况最详细的披露。

sentences.en: The documents reveal that Anthropic's revenue has skyrocketed in the first half of this year to more than $16 billion, a 14-fold increase from a year earlier.
sentences.zh: 文件显示，Anthropic的收入在今年上半年飙升至超过160亿美元，比一年前增长了14倍。
